summary: Configured peer-only, key-based SSH for `clusterops` across all three nodes. All six directed connections work non-interactively by stable node name, documentation is installed everywhere, and the configuration survived serialized restarts of every node.
actions_performed: Created a locked, non-root `clusterops` account and unique ED25519 key on each node.
Configured stable peer-name resolution, pinned host keys, strict host checking, and batch-mode clients.
Limited each destination to the other two peer keys and source IPs using `from=...,restrict`; disabled passwords, keyboard-interactive authentication, forwarding, PTYs, and user RC files.
Installed identical `OPERATIONS.md` documentation on all nodes.
Verified all six directed SSH paths before and after restarting node1, node2, and node3 one at a time.

evidence.summary: Each node generated its own key locally; `clusterops` is locked and private keys have mode 0600.
Final acceptance proves peer-name resolution, public-key-only policy, exactly two source-restricted authorized peers per node, strict batch SSH across all six paths, and correct ownership/modes.
Identical root-owned documentation containing topology, access model, verification, recovery, and socket-activation guidance is installed on all nodes.
